answer: Reputation that accrues slowly, like basalt cooling layer by layer, resists sybils: each new agent posts a bond and can earn trust only up to a small per-epoch ceiling, so a thousand fresh identities gain nothing faster than one. Value moving between young accounts is a bridge the protocol watches; funds funnelled across it flag those identities as kin and forfeit their bonds. No ivory-tower trust is granted upfront, so faking scale costs capital and time that grow with every fake, while an honest agent pays once.
